questions.prompt: What does RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) mean in C++?

options.text: Tying resource lifetime (memory, files, mutexes) to object lifetime so the destructor always releases it

questions.prompt: Which smart pointer represents exclusive, single-owner heap ownership with zero reference-counting overhead?
Why is `std::make_unique<T>(args...)` preferred over `std::unique_ptr<T>(new T(args...))`?

options.text: It avoids explicit `new` and prevents potential leaks in pre-C++17 multi-argument expressions

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `std::shared_ptr` and `std::weak_ptr`. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `std::weak_ptr` observes a `shared_ptr`-managed object without incrementing the strong reference count
`std::weak_ptr` can be dereferenced directly without calling `.lock()`
`std::shared_ptr` uses an atomic reference count to track shared ownership
Two `shared_ptr`s pointing to each other create a reference cycle that leaks memory

questions.prompt: Match each C++ cast operator to its intended use.

columns.label: Well-defined compile-time conversions (numeric, base/derived without runtime check)
Adding or removing `const`/`volatile` qualifiers (UB to mutate truly `const` objects)

questions.prompt: Why MUST a polymorphic base class have a `virtual` destructor?

options.text: So `delete basePtr` invokes the derived class's destructor before freeing memory, avoiding UB

questions.prompt: What does the `override` specifier on a derived method guarantee?

options.text: Causes a compile error if the method does not actually override a `virtual` base method (catching signature typos)

questions.prompt: What makes a C++ class an abstract class that cannot be instantiated directly?

options.text: Containing at least one pure virtual function (`= 0`)

questions.prompt: What is the Rule of Zero in modern C++?

options.text: Classes that don't directly manage raw resources should define no custom destructor or copy/move ops, relying on RAII members

questions.prompt: According to the Rule of Five, if a class defines a custom destructor (to manage a raw resource), what else should it usually define or `= default`/`= delete`?

options.text: Copy constructor, copy assignment, move constructor, and move assignment

questions.prompt: What does `std::move(x)` actually do at runtime?

options.text: Nothing at runtime—it is an unconditional cast of `x` to an rvalue reference (`T&&`) so move overloads can steal resources

questions.prompt: What is iterator invalidation in `std::vector`?

options.text: `push_back` or `insert` that triggers reallocation invalidates all existing pointers, references, and iterators into the vector

questions.prompt: How does `std::unordered_map` differ from `std::map`?

options.text: `unordered_map` uses a hash table ($O(1)$ average lookup); `map` uses a balanced tree ($O(\log n)$ sorted lookup)

questions.prompt: Select all valid lambda capture clauses in C++. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `[&]` captures used outer variables by reference
`[x, &y]` captures `x` by value and `y` by reference
`[&x]` keeps `x` alive forever even after its stack frame returns
`[=]` captures used outer variables by value

questions.prompt: What does `std::optional<T>` represent?

options.text: A value of type `T` that may or may not be present, without heap allocation

questions.prompt: What is `std::variant<int, std::string>`?

options.text: A type-safe tagged union holding one of a fixed set of alternative types at a time

questions.prompt: What does structured binding `for (const auto& [key, val] : my_map)` do in C++17?

options.text: Unpacks each `std::pair` entry into named references `key` and `val`

questions.prompt: Why should move constructors and move assignment operators be marked `noexcept` when possible?

options.text: `std::vector` will only move elements during reallocation if the move constructor is `noexcept` (otherwise it falls back to copying for strong exception safety)
It is required by the linker

questions.prompt: What is object slicing in C++?

options.text: Assigning or passing a `Derived` object by value to a `Base` parameter, stripping away derived fields and `virtual` dispatch

questions.prompt: Match each STL associative container to its key property.

columns.label: Sorted unique keys with no separate mapped value

questions.prompt: What does `template <typename T> T max_val(T a, T b)` generate?

options.text: Type-safe function instantiations at compile time for each concrete `T` used

questions.prompt: Why are template definitions normally placed in header files rather than `.cpp` files?

options.text: The compiler needs the full template body when instantiating it in each translation unit that uses a new `T`

questions.prompt: What does `v.emplace_back(arg1, arg2)` do compared to `v.push_back(Obj(arg1, arg2))`?

options.text: Constructs `Obj` directly in-place inside `v`'s buffer, avoiding a temporary object and move

questions.prompt: What does `std::unique_ptr::release()` do vs `.reset()`?

options.text: `.release()` relinquishes ownership and returns the raw pointer WITHOUT deleting it; `.reset()` deletes the managed object

questions.prompt: Select all operations that are safe on a moved-from standard library object (like `std::string` or `std::vector`). (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Destroying it when it leaves scope
Assigning a new value to it (`s = "new";`)
Calling `.clear()` to reset it to a known empty state
Assuming it still contains its original pre-move elements

questions.prompt: What does `std::deque<T>` support efficiently that `std::vector<T>` does not?

options.text: $O(1)$ insertion and removal at BOTH front (`push_front`) and back (`push_back`)

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `std::erase_if(vec, pred)` (C++20) or the erase-remove idiom (`vec.erase(std::remove_if(...), vec.end())`)?

options.text: Removes matching elements from a container and shrinks its size in linear time

questions.prompt: What does `final` on a class or virtual method (`void f() override final;`) prevent?

options.text: Any further subclass from inheriting the class or overriding `f()`

questions.prompt: What does `std::array<int, 4>` offer over `int a[4]`?

options.text: Value semantics (copyable/returnable), `.size()`, `.at()`, and no silent decay to `int *`

questions.prompt: What does `std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mtx);` guarantee?

options.text: Prevents all data races in the whole program
Acquires `mtx` on construction and automatically unlocks it when `lock` leaves scope

questions.prompt: What happens when `std::map::operator[]` (`m["missing"]`) is called for a key not yet in `m`?

options.text: Inserts a default-constructed value for `"missing"` and returns a reference to it

questions.prompt: What is a copy-and-swap idiom used for in `operator=`?

options.text: Providing clean, self-assignment-safe, strong exception-safe copy assignment using the copy constructor and `swap`

questions.prompt: Match each C++11/17/20 utility type to what it models.

columns.label: Zero or one value of type `T`
Exactly one value from a fixed set of types

questions.prompt: What does `mutable` on a non-static class member allow?

options.text: Modifying that member even inside a `const` member function (e.g., for an internal `std::mutex` or cache)

questions.prompt: What is `std::make_shared<T>(args...)` primarily optimizing over `std::shared_ptr<T>(new T(args...))`?

options.text: Allocates the `T` object and the `shared_ptr` control block in a single heap allocation

questions.prompt: When does `std::vector::reserve(n)` help performance?

options.text: When you want to shrink memory
When you know the approximate element count upfront, avoiding repeated reallocations and element moves during `push_back`

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways to iterate or search with `<algorithm>` / `<ranges>` in modern C++. (Select all that apply.)
What does `[[nodiscard]]` on a function or type warn about in C++17+?

options.text: Ignoring the return value of the function at a call site (e.g., an error code or newly allocated handle)

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `std::thread::join()`?

options.text: Blocks the calling thread until the target thread finishes execution
Detaches the thread as a daemon

questions.prompt: What does `std::async` + `std::future<T>` provide?

options.text: A higher-level way to run a task and retrieve its return value (or rethrow its exception) via `.get()`

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about header-only vs compiled `.cpp` dependencies. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Forward declarations (`class Foo;`) in headers can reduce `#include` coupling when only pointers/references are used
Every `.cpp` file must `#include` all other `.cpp` files
Moving stable non-template implementation details into `.cpp` files reduces rebuild times across dependents
Header-only templates can increase compile times when included widely

questions.prompt: What does `if (auto it = m.find(k); it != m.end())` (C++17 if-with-initializer) improve?

options.text: Limits `it`'s scope strictly to the `if`/`else` block so it doesn't leak into surrounding code
